commitResults.messageBody:

commitResults.messageTitle: Validate student names using the feature spec rules
commitResults.messageBody:
Follow the F1 rules in the Week 6 feature spec: names are 1 to 50
characters, contain at least one letter, and use only letters
(including accented and non-Latin letters), spaces, hyphens,
apostrophes or full stops. This accepts names such as O'Brien,
Mary-Anne and José, which AB3 rejected, and rejects digits.

Repeated spaces between words are reduced to one when parsing, so
'John   Tan' is stored as 'John Tan' instead of being rejected.

Add 'student view n/NAME' (F2), which shows a student's name and
subjects, or '(none recorded)' if there are none. The name is matched
ignoring case and extra spaces through Model#findStudentByName, and an
unknown name gives "No student named '<name>' found."

The command only reads data; it does not change the student list.

commitResults.messageTitle: Use feature spec messages for student add and view
commitResults.messageBody:
Match the F1 and F2 outputs in the Week 6 feature spec:

* student add shows '✔ Student added: NAME (subjects: ...)' or
  '(no subjects recorded)', followed by the total number of students.
* A duplicate name gives "A student named 'NAME' already exists.
  Student names must be unique."
* Format errors for student add and student view show the command
  format, e.g. 'Command format: student add n/NAME [s/SUBJECT]...'.

Every error shown in the result display now starts with ❌, so all
commands, including later interaction and follow-up commands, follow
the team's message rule without extra code.

commitResults.messageTitle: Normalize student names to Unicode NFC
commitResults.messageBody:
A composed "é" and an "e" followed by a combining accent look the
same but compared as different names, so TutorLink could hold two
visually identical students.

Store every Name in NFC form and check the length limit on that
form. Lookup, duplicate detection, display and the data file then
all use one spelling, and two such names in a saved file are
rejected as duplicates on load. find also composes its keywords.

commitResults.messageTitle: Turn pasted line breaks into spaces
commitResults.messageBody:

"line two" on separate lines joined them into "line oneline two"
without any message. Replace each line break with a space before
the text reaches the command box, and say so in the UG instead of
the single-line error that could never appear in the app.

commitResults.messageTitle: Warn and back up when the data file is unreadable
commitResults.messageBody:
An invalid data file made TutorLink start with no students and no
message, and the next change overwrote the file, losing the data.

Copy the unreadable file to tutorlink.json.bak before anything can
overwrite it, and show a warning naming the backup in the result
box. If the copy fails, the warning says so instead. Update the UG
caution to describe this and how to recover.

commitResults.messageTitle: Separate startup warning messages from VERSION
commitResults.messageBody: Keep a blank line between VERSION and the new message constants so this change merges cleanly with the version update in #139.
Add coverage for null stored subjects

commitResults.messageTitle: Enable assertions when running the app
commitResults.messageBody:
Assertions were off for ./gradlew run, so assert statements in the
code were never checked outside the tests. The course requires them
to be enabled from v1.4.

Turn them on for the Gradle run task, and tell developers to add -ea
to the IDEA run configuration. Also fix the main class name in the
setup guide, which still pointed to seedu.address.Main.

Fixes #147

Tutors cannot correct a student's name or subjects without deleting
the student, which also deletes their interactions and follow-ups
(US05).

Add student edit n/NAME [new/NEW_NAME] [s/SUBJECT]..., as agreed for
v1.4: at least one of new/ or s/ is needed, any s/ replaces all
subjects, and renaming to another existing name is rejected as a
duplicate. Interactions and follow-ups are kept, and the panels
update if the student is selected. Document it in the User Guide.

Fixes #146

commitResults.messageTitle: Update the Storage class diagram for TutorLink
commitResults.messageBody:
The DG's Storage diagram and text still described AB3's address book
classes (JsonAddressBookStorage, JsonAdaptedPerson, JsonAdaptedTag),
which no longer exist.

Show the TutorLink storage classes instead, including the adapters for
interactions and follow-ups, regenerate the PNG, and point the API
link and component text at the TutorLink code.

Fixes #150

commitResults.messageTitle: Test student edit equality and toString
commitResults.messageBody:
Codecov flagged the toString method and one equals branch of
EditStudentCommand as untested. Cover both so the PR does not lower
coverage.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add assertions and logging to student commands
commitResults.messageBody:
The student add, view and delete commands leave no trace in the log
and do not check their own assumptions about the model.

Log each successful run at INFO through LogsCenter, and assert that
an added student is stored and that a deleted student is gone and no
longer selected. User input is still validated with exceptions.

commitResults.messageTitle: Document student edit in the Developer Guide
commitResults.messageBody:
The DG did not explain how student edit works or why it replaces all
subjects, and testers had no manual test cases for it.

Add an "Editing a student" implementation section with a sequence
diagram and design considerations, and add manual test cases for
renaming, replacing subjects and invalid edits.

Fixes #158

commitResults.messageTitle: Test assertion failures in student commands
commitResults.messageBody:
The new assertions in AddCommand and DeleteCommand were only checked
on their passing side, so a broken model would go untested.

Add model stubs that fail to store an added student, fail to remove a
deleted one, or leave a deleted student selected, and check that each
case raises the expected AssertionError.

commitResults.messageTitle: Clear selection when an edit hides the student
commitResults.messageBody:
After find tan and student view n/John Tan, renaming John Tan to a
name that no longer matches the filter removed him from the list but
left him selected, so the panels showed a student the list did not.

Make ModelManager#setStudent apply the same check as
updateFilteredStudentList: if the edited student is no longer in the
filtered list, clear the selection. Add tests for renames that still
match the filter and renames that do not.

Also replace the UG tip that told users to delete and re-add a student
to fix their details, which loses their records, with student edit.

commitResults.messageTitle: Describe selection clearing in the student edit DG
commitResults.messageBody:
Student edit now clears the selection when the edited student no
longer matches the active find filter. Say so in the implementation
steps and add a manual test case for it.

commitResults.messageTitle: Show all students when viewing a hidden one
commitResults.messageBody:
After `find lim`, `student view n/john tan` selected John Tan and
showed him in the panels, but the filter still hid him from the
student list.

ModelManager#setSelectedStudent now resets the filter to show all
students when the given student is hidden. This keeps the selected
student inside the filtered list for every caller, matching how
updateFilteredStudentList already clears a hidden selection.

Add regression tests for an active filter with the student hidden or
shown, and for a hidden student with interactions and follow-ups.
Document the behaviour in the UG and DG.
Add follow-up status and persistence support
Add follow-up completion command

# Conflicts:
#	src/main/java/seedu/tutorlink/logic/parser/CliSyntax.java
#	src/main/java/seedu/tutorlink/logic/parser/TutorLinkParser.java

commitResults.messageTitle: Check full student state in command assertions
commitResults.messageBody:
The add assertion only checked that a student with the same name
exists, so a model that dropped the subjects would pass. The delete
assertion used equals, so a stale selected copy with other subjects
would pass too.

Compare the stored student with the added one in full, and check the
selection by student identity after a delete.
Add interaction deletion command
Add interaction edit command
Add TutorLink delete sequence diagram

# Conflicts:
#	src/main/java/seedu/tutorlink/logic/parser/TutorLinkParser.java
#	src/test/java/seedu/tutorlink/logic/parser/TutorLinkParserTest.java
Add follow-up cancellation command
Update model follow-up status

# Conflicts:
#	docs/DeveloperGuide.md
#	src/test/java/seedu/tutorlink/logic/commands/SelectedStudentFilterTest.java

commitResults.messageTitle: Test clearing selection while a filter is active
commitResults.messageBody:
setSelectedStudent(null) skips the filter reset because there is no
student to show. Cover that path: select a shown student under an
active find filter, clear the selection, and check that the selection
is null and the filtered list is unchanged.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add DG use cases for student commands
commitResults.messageBody:
The only student use case was AB3's "Delete a person", which refers
to listing persons and deleting by index. TutorLink has no persons and
identifies students by name.

Replace it with use cases for adding, viewing, editing and deleting a
student, matching the current commands and their error handling.

Fixes #174

commitResults.messageTitle: Replace AB3 names in the DG design sections
commitResults.messageBody:
The architecture, UI, Logic and common-classes sections still named
AB3 classes such as PersonListPanel, AddressBookParser and the
seedu.address package, linked to the AB3 repository, and used
"delete 1" as the example. DevOps.md named addressbook.jar.

Use the TutorLink names, link to the team repository, and update the
UI, parser and architecture diagrams to match the code.

Fixes #175

commitResults.messageTitle: Remove outdated note from the README
commitResults.messageBody:
The README said the guides were still moving from AddressBook toward
the planned TutorLink features. All v1.4 features are now in, so the
note no longer applies.

commitResults.messageTitle: Remove AB3 proposed features from the DG
commitResults.messageBody:
The DG still had AB3's sample "[Proposed] Undo/redo feature", which
describes VersionedAddressBook and AB3 commands such as "delete 5" and
"add n/David", and an empty "[Proposed] Data archiving" placeholder.
TutorLink plans neither feature.

Remove both sections, the nine undo/redo diagrams they used, and the
unreferenced AB3 BetterModelClassDiagram.

Fixes #173
Reject trailing JSON content
Remove AB3 proposed features from the DG

Resolve the User Guide conflict with #182 by keeping both the time
removal sentence and the renumbering warning. Removing or changing a
time can also reorder interactions, so the warning now mentions time.
Fix F3/F4 persistence handling

commitResults.messageTitle: Test student commands after failed saves
commitResults.messageBody:
The fix for #184 and #185 in #187 had regression tests for the
follow-up commands only (#189, #190). Nothing checked that the student
commands roll back a failed save or that student view does not save.

Cover student add, edit and delete with I/O and permission failures,
check that a later successful save does not persist the failed change,
and check that student view works with a read-only data file without
trying to save.

Fixes #191

MainApp.VERSION still said V1.3, so the log would report the wrong
version for the v1.4 release.

commitResults.messageTitle: Correct the UG answer on moving data
commitResults.messageBody:
The FAQ said running TutorLink once creates data/tutorlink.json. Since
#187, TutorLink only writes the file after a command that changes
data, so a fresh install that is only opened has no file to replace.

Tell users to copy the data folder next to the JAR on the new
computer instead. Also drop "home folder", since the data folder sits
next to the JAR file.
Add interaction time removal

commitResults.messageTitle: Start read-only success messages with a tick
commitResults.messageBody:
Standardisation rule 6 says every success message starts with a tick,
but list, find, help, student view, interaction list and followup list
showed plain text, so their results looked different from the other
commands.

Add the tick to these six messages and to the matching UG examples.
Informational messages that start with the info sign are unchanged.

Fixes #195

commitResults.messageTitle: Reword startup log for a missing data file
commitResults.messageBody:
The log said a new data file was being created, but none is written
at startup. Since #187 the file is only created after the first
command that changes data, so say that instead.

Fixes #197

commitResults.messageTitle: Allow s/o and d/o in student names
commitResults.messageBody:
Names such as "Raj s/o Kumar" are common in Singapore, but the "s/o"
was read as the s/ prefix, so the name was cut short and "o Kumar"
was saved as a subject.

Treat a standalone "s/o" or "d/o" word as part of the value when
tokenizing, and accept these connectors in Name.

Fixes #199

commitResults.messageTitle: Name unknown parameters in error messages
commitResults.messageBody:
A parameter that a command does not take, such as x/ in
"student add n/Ann x/foo", was kept as part of the name. The user then
saw the name rules, although the name itself was valid.

When a name, subject, index, date or time is invalid, check it for a
later word that looks like a parameter and report that word instead.

Fixes #200

commitResults.messageTitle: Suggest commands for an incomplete command word
commitResults.messageBody:
Typing only "student", "interaction" or "followup", or an unknown
action such as "student fly", gave "Unknown command." with no hint
about which commands exist.

List the commands of that group in the error message instead.

Fixes #201

commitResults.messageTitle: Show the valid range for an out-of-range index
commitResults.messageBody:
"Index exceeds the number of available items." did not say how many
items there were, or that the list was empty. Completing the last
follow-up and then running "followup done" again gave no hint that
nothing was left.

Name the student and the valid range instead, or say that the student
has no interactions or no outstanding follow-ups.

Fixes #202

commitResults.messageTitle: Match the find usage message to other commands
commitResults.messageBody:
The find usage message still used the AB3 wording, mentioned index
numbers that TutorLink does not use, and did not start with
"Command format:" like every other command.

Fixes #203

commitResults.messageTitle: Reject a student edit that changes nothing
commitResults.messageBody:
"student edit n/Bob new/Bob" reported "Student updated" although the
name and subjects stayed the same. Tell the user that nothing changed
instead.

Fixes #204

commitResults.messageTitle: Share the subject wording of add and edit
commitResults.messageBody:
student add showed "(no subjects recorded)" but student edit showed
"(subjects: (none recorded))" for the same state. Both commands now
describe subjects with the same AddCommand helper.

Fixes #205

commitResults.messageTitle: Accept an empty t/ in interaction add
commitResults.messageBody:
interaction edit treats "t/" with no value as "no time", but
interaction add rejected it with "Interaction time must be a valid
time in HH:mm format." Record the interaction without a time instead,
so both commands read t/ the same way.

Fixes #206

commitResults.messageTitle: Add missing setup notes and known issues to UG
commitResults.messageBody:
The Week 11 checklist asks the UG to warn that double-clicking the
JAR may not work and that the app cannot save from a write-protected
folder. Add both, and name the data file location using the same
"home folder" term as the Quick start.

commitResults.messageTitle: Replace DG placeholders with real content
commitResults.messageBody:
Fill in the remaining "More to be added" use cases for editing and
deleting interactions, completing and cancelling follow-ups, and
finding students. Close the dangling future-date extension.

In the manual tests, launch with java -jar instead of double-clicking,
add a shutdown test in place of the template placeholder, and expect
the .bak backup that the app now makes for a corrupted data file.

commitResults.messageTitle: Document help window behavior in macOS full screen
commitResults.messageBody:
On macOS, when TutorLink is in full-screen mode, the help window opens
in its own full-screen space. Closing it returns to the desktop rather
than to TutorLink, which stays open in its own space. Tested manually.
